typical_symptoms: Absence of chlorotic or necrotic leaf spots
Fully expanded, well-formed palmate leaves with intact margins
Vigorous stem and petiole growth without vascular discoloration or dark lesions
Normal boll development without rot or sunken lesions
visual_characteristics: Uniform light green to dark green leaf lamina
Clean, distinct vein patterns without interveinal or vein-clearing chlorosis
Fine, natural pubescence (trichomes) visible on the underside and veins
Turgid and smooth leaf surface with no curling, cupping, or wilting
color_characteristics: Consistent green foliage ranging from bright green to deep forest green
Normal light green or pinkish-red hue on mature petioles and stems exposed to sunlight
No abnormal yellowing, bronzing, purpling, or dark brown/black discoloration
texture_characteristics: Slightly velvety or puberulent leaf surface due to healthy trichomes
Firm leaf blade tissue without dry, brittle, or water-soaked regions
spatial_patterns: Uniform green tone across all leaf lobes
Absence of concentric rings, scattered spotting, or localized blotches
Clean interveinal regions with no chlorotic streaking
distinguishing_features: Complete absence of visible foliar symptoms, fungal mats, or bacterial oozing
Symmetrical palmate leaf morphology with clear, healthy venation
Consistent canopy color density and active turgor pressure
commonly_confused_with: Early-stage nutrient deficiencies (e.g., mild nitrogen or potassium deficiency)
Minor mechanical wind or hail damage
Slight chemical spray drift or herbicidal injury
